title: Segmented Housing Search
key_point: Trulia alerts: all set geography, 2/3 price, 1/3 baths; median price band ±27%; restaurants/bars explain 25.3% of area popularity, schools 2.6%.

title: How website users segment a city: The geography of housing search in London
key_point: ~100k Rightmove drawn searches: 50% under 5 km2, smaller than a borough; 51.5% omit bedrooms; 2-bed £250-500k most pressured.

title: Online housing search: A gravity model approach
key_point: 1.1bn Funda hits: 1% more distance cuts search flows 1.1%; own municipality +176%, neighbours +71%; gravity explains ~80%.

title: Internet search behavior, liquidity and prices in the housing market
publisher: De Nederlandsche Bank WP 481 (Real Estate Economics)
key_point: Funda clicks per listing over supply Granger-cause liquidity then prices; demand shocks hit sale speed first, prices permanently later.

title: Housing Search Frictions: Evidence from Detailed Search Data and a Field Experiment
key_point: School info on listings shifted moves to 0.10 SD better schools; families trade 54 commute minutes per 10 school percentiles.

title: Human-Algorithm Interactions: Evidence from Zillow.com
key_point: 1% higher Zestimate raises list price 0.733% and sold price 0.081%; feedback shocks fade as marginal effects are below one.

title: Housing Search in the Age of Big Data: Smarter Cities or the Same Old Blind Spots?
key_point: Craigslist listings over-represent whiter, richer tracts; poor minority tracts 7-9 points less likely to show exact address.

title: Auditing Race and Gender Discrimination in Online Housing Markets
key_point: Sock-puppet audit: Realtor.com personalised ranking showed women pricier homes first; white profiles saw more housing ads.

title: The new 'lettings agent's window': interface design and discrimination on online rental platforms
key_point: 96% of UK renters use Rightmove/SpareRoom/Zoopla/Gumtree; removing SpareRoom 'No DSS' tool raised benefit-open listings from 9% to 48%.

title: Rental Rooms: Spaces of Migrant Housing, Overcrowding, and Social Reproduction in the Rentier City
key_point: London migrants find rooms via Facebook/WhatsApp groups, co-ethnic contacts; trade space for price and proximity to work; 75% recent migrants rent privately.

title: Social discourse, housing search and residential segregation: economic migrants in Seville
key_point: Migrants initially avoid enclaves but owner/agent rejection and co-national job networks pull them in; transport links valued.

title: Residential location choice and its effects on travel satisfaction in a context of short-term transnational relocation
publisher: Journal of Transport and Land Use (Monteiro et al.)
key_point: Porto newcomers trading distance for lower rent report lower satisfaction; information gaps on outer-area transport drive dissonant choices.

title: AI: Real Estate's New Roommate - The Good, the Bad, and the Algorithmic
publisher: Journal of Property Investment & Finance (Real Estate Insights)
key_point: ML personalises portal search and AVMs give first-pass valuations; LLMs need human checks; bias and depersonalisation are key risks.

title: Realtor.com launches RealAssistAI powered by Google
key_point: Conversational search handles affordability, neighbourhood, commute, schools, parks; remembers budget and priorities across sessions.

title: Redfin Debuts Conversational Search to Reinvent How You Find Homes
key_point: Conversational search users view ~2x listings, search broader areas with specific features, 47% more likely to request tours.

title: A Unified Framework for Measuring Preferences for Schools and Neighborhoods
key_point: Boundary design: 5% better school performance raises prices under 1%; neighbour-demographic premia mostly reflect unobserved quality.

title: What's in a Grade? School Report Cards and the Housing Market
key_point: Arbitrary school letter-grade distinctions caused major house price effects; information framing matters.

title: Sorting or Steering: The Effects of Housing Discrimination on Neighborhood Choice
key_point: HUD audits in 28 cities: minority testers steered to areas with worse schools, more poverty, crime and pollution.

title: Testing for Information Asymmetries in Real Estate Markets
key_point: Sellers know neighbourhood trajectories better than buyers and time sales; more informed sellers predict later price falls.

title: Expecting Climate Change: A Nationwide Field Experiment in the Housing Market
key_point: Showing flood risk to 17.5m Redfin users changed search, bids, purchases; buyers traded amenities for lower risk.

title: The Geography of Algorithmic Judgment: LLM Intermediaries, Place Identity, and Racial Steering in Housing Search
key_point: Seven LLMs across four US cities show inconsistent, city-dependent racial steering, often amplified by preference-laden prompts.
